bib.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

question: Can a better dense passage retriever for open-domain QA be trained using only question-passage pairs, without extra retrieval-specific pretraining, and does it beat BM25?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning two BERT encoders on existing question-passage pairs with a suitable negative-sampling scheme is enough to beat BM25, and higher retrieval accuracy translates into higher end-to-end QA accuracy.
contributions: With the proper training setup, simply fine-tuning question and passage encoders on existing question-passage pairs greatly outperforms BM25, with no additional pretraining.
Higher retrieval precision translates to higher end-to-end QA accuracy, giving comparable or better results on multiple open-retrieval QA datasets.

method.summary: Two independent BERT-base uncased encoders (question, passage) map text to 768-d [CLS] vectors scored by dot product, trained with a negative log-likelihood loss over one positive, in-batch gold negatives and one BM25 hard negative. Passages (21M, 100 words) are indexed offline with FAISS. An extractive BERT reader with passage selection reranks the top-k for end-to-end QA.
method.task: open-domain question answering (passage retrieval and extractive reading)

datasets.name: English Wikipedia passage corpus
datasets.source: Wikipedia dump of Dec. 20, 2018, cleaned with DrQA preprocessing; each passage prepended with article title and [SEP]
datasets.preprocessing: tables, infoboxes, lists and disambiguation pages removed; disjoint 100-word blocks; overlapping passages not advantageous

datasets.name: Natural Questions
datasets.preprocessing: gold passage matched to the candidate pool; discarded if matching failed

datasets.name: TriviaQA
datasets.preprocessing: positive = highest-ranked BM25 passage containing the answer; dropped if none in top 100

datasets.name: SQuAD v1.1
datasets.preprocessing: gold passage matched to the candidate pool

models.name: DPR question and passage encoders
models.architecture: two independent BERT-base uncased dual encoders, [CLS] output, d = 768, dot-product similarity

other.index: FAISS HNSW on CPU, neighbors per node 512, construction search depth 200, search depth 128

models.name: Reader
models.architecture: BERT base uncased; start/end span scores and passage selection from [CLS] vectors

training.objective: negative log likelihood of the positive passage (softmax over positive and negatives) with in-batch negatives; 1 BM25 hard negative per question shared across the batch
training.epochs: up to 40 for NQ, TriviaQA, SQuAD; 100 for TREC, WQ
training.hardware: reader experiments on eight 32GB GPUs; retriever training hardware not stated

other.multi_setting: one encoder trained on all datasets except SQuAD
other.reader_negatives: 1 positive and 23 negatives sampled from top 100 (m~ = 24)
other.reader_loss: marginal log-likelihood of correct spans in the positive passage plus log-likelihood of positive passage selected
other.reader_k: tuned on dev; k = 50 optimal for NQ
other.multi_reader: for WQ and TREC in Multi, the NQ-trained reader is fine-tuned to the target
other.hyperparameters_note: Appendix B says the analysis experiments use a better hyper-parameter setting documented in the code release, not given in the paper

inference.decoding: extractive: best span from the passage with the highest passage selection score
inference.samples: single run; no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: top-k by inner product via FAISS HNSW; reader takes up to 100 passages; hybrid reranks the union of BM25 top-2000 and DPR top-2000 by BM25(q,p) + lambda * sim(q,p) with lambda = 1.1 chosen on dev

metrics.name: Top-k retrieval accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions for which the top-k retrieved passages contain a span that answers the question (answer string match)

metrics.name: Exact match (EM)
metrics.definition: exact match with the reference answer after minor normalization (Chen et al. 2017; Lee et al. 2019)

baselines: REALM Wiki and News (Guu et al. 2020)
eval.protocol: retrieval on test sets (Table 2) and NQ dev for ablations (Table 3); end-to-end EM on test sets; single run, no significance test stated

availability.weights: trained models released at the same repository
availability.data: public QA datasets and Wikipedia dump

results.claim: DPR beats BM25 at top-20 on Natural Questions test by a large margin.
results.setup: NQ test, single-dataset DPR, 21M-passage Wikipedia index, BERT-base dual encoder
results.quote: The gap is especially large when k is small (e.g., 78.4% vs. 59.1% for top-20 accuracy on Natural Questions)

results.claim: Across datasets other than SQuAD, DPR beats BM25 by 9 to 19 points absolute at top-20.
results.setup: five test sets; the abstract range
results.quote: by 9%-19% absolute in terms of top-20 passage retrieval accuracy
results.note: Table 2 Single DPR minus BM25 at top-20: NQ 19.3, TriviaQA 12.5, WQ 18.2, TREC 8.9, SQuAD -5.6

results.claim: DPR beats BM25 at top-5 on NQ.
results.quote: outperforms BM25 by a large margin (65.2% vs. 42.9% in Top-5 accuracy)
results.note: The split (test or dev) is not stated at this point in the text

results.claim: End-to-end NQ exact match is higher with DPR than with ORQA.
results.setup: open NQ, DPR retriever (Single or Multi, same value) plus BERT reader, k = 50
results.quote: (41.5% vs. 33.3%) in the open Natural Questions
results.table: Table 4, row Single DPR, column NQ

results.claim: BM25 beats single-dataset DPR on SQuAD at top-20.
results.setup: SQuAD test; authors attribute it to high lexical overlap (questions written after seeing the passage) and a narrow set of 500+ articles
results.table: Table 2, row Single DPR, column SQuAD Top-20

results.claim: In-batch negatives raise NQ dev top-20 over 1-of-N training with the same 7 gold negatives.
results.setup: NQ dev, Gold negatives, #N = 7, with vs without IB
results.table: Table 3, rows Gold 7 (without IB 63.1; with IB 69.1), column Top-20

results.claim: Accuracy rises with the number of in-batch negatives.
results.setup: NQ dev, Gold in-batch, 127 negatives vs 7

results.claim: Adding one BM25 hard negative per question lifts NQ dev top-20 substantially.
results.setup: NQ dev, in-batch 127 gold + 128 BM25 negatives (1 per question) vs 127 gold only
results.note: A second BM25 negative did not help: 76.4 vs 77.3 at 31 gold

results.claim: A second BM25 negative does not help further.
results.quote: adding a single BM25 negative passage improves the result substantially while adding two does not help further

results.claim: 1,000 training examples already beat BM25 on NQ dev.
results.setup: NQ dev, Figure 1, number of training examples varied 1k to 59k
results.note: Values read from a plot only; no numbers given

results.claim: Linear BM25+DPR combination helps on TREC and SQuAD and costs a little on NQ (Single).
results.setup: TREC test, Single; BM25+DPR vs DPR; lambda = 1.1; SQuAD 71.5 vs 63.2; NQ 76.6 vs 78.4
results.table: Table 2, row Single BM25 + DPR, column TREC Top-20

results.claim: Training on multiple datasets greatly helps the smallest dataset, TREC.
results.setup: TREC test; Multi vs Single DPR; SQuAD excluded from Multi training and gets worse (51.6 vs 63.2)
results.table: Table 2, row Multi DPR, column TREC Top-20

results.claim: DPR trained on NQ alone generalizes to WQ and TREC with a 3-5 point loss versus fine-tuned, still far above BM25.
results.setup: NQ-trained DPR tested on WebQuestions / TREC; best fine-tuned 75.0/89.1

results.claim: Distant supervision (BM25 positive) costs about 1 point versus gold-context positives.
results.table: Table 5, row Dist. Sup., column Top-20

results.claim: L2 and triplet loss do not beat dot product with NLL on NQ dev.
results.setup: NQ dev; L2 + NLL 76.1, triplet + dot product 77.2, L2 + triplet 78.1
results.table: Table 6, row L2 NLL, column Top-20
results.note: Cosine is stated inferior but no number is given

results.claim: DPR retrieval is about 42 times faster per second than Lucene BM25 per CPU thread, but indexing is far slower.
results.setup: Intel Xeon E5-2698 v4 2.20GHz, 512GB; DPR with FAISS HNSW in memory, top 100 per question; BM25 in Java with file index, per CPU thread
results.note: Embedding 21M passages about 8.8 hours on 8 GPUs; FAISS index build 8.5 hours; Lucene inverted index about 30 minutes

results.claim: A joint retriever-reader training scheme gives the same NQ dev EM as the pipeline.
results.setup: NQ dev; passage encoder fixed, only question encoder trained jointly

results.claim: Reading only 10 passages costs under one EM point on NQ.

limits: Retrieval is evaluated by answer-string containment in the top-k, not by relevance judgments.
SQuAD is an exception where BM25 wins; authors attribute it to lexical overlap and a biased article set, and SQuAD is excluded from Multi training.
Qualitative analysis (Appendix C) shows DPR may lack capacity to represent rare salient phrases (Thoros of Myr example).
Single runs; no seeds or variance stated; retriever training hardware, warmup steps and weight decay not stated.
Table 3 numbers are with older hyper-parameters; Tables 5 and 6 baselines (NQ dev top-20 78.1) use better ones from the code release (Appendix B).
Index build time is long (8.8 h embeddings on 8 GPUs plus 8.5 h FAISS vs about 30 min Lucene).
The authors say it is not clear how much more inference time the reader takes versus ORQA.
